title: Peter Simpson, the England coach who guided John Hilton to the 1980 European title, dies aged 92
seo_title: Peter Simpson, former England table tennis coach, dies at 92
description: Peter Simpson, who coached John Hilton to the 1980 European men's singles title and led England's men to European team silver, has died at the age of 92.
standfirst: The Leeds tailor turned national coach captained England at the World and European Championships and was made a Table Tennis England vice-president in 2024.
body: Peter Simpson, the former England coach who guided John Hilton to the men's singles title at the 1980 European Championships, has died at the age of 92, Table Tennis England announced on Thursday.

Simpson coached England through one of the strongest spells in the country's history. As well as Hilton's singles title in Bern, he led the men's team of Hilton, Desmond Douglas, Nicky Jarvis and Paul Day to silver at the European Championships in 1978, and Hilton, Douglas and Day added team bronze in 1980.

Hilton, known for an unorthodox style with what he calls his "dodgy" bat, paid tribute to his former coach. "He was a very mild-mannered man, very easy to get on with and didn't rush things at all. He was very thorough and his heart was in the right place," he said.

Hilton said Simpson kept the squad guessing over selection until a few hours before matches, so that everyone practised and prepared properly. He added that his own style was so instinctive that there was little a coach could tell him mid-match: "But he was a calming influence and I think he was great at that 'less is better' approach rather than bombard you with information."
## From Leeds tailor to national coach

Simpson was born in Leeds in 1934 and started playing at the All Souls Youth Club at 15, the age at which he left school to become a tailor, a trade he followed for 20 years. At Leeds Central YMCA he met his lifelong mentor, Alan Thompson, who introduced him to coaching, and after joining the Victoria club in 1951 he worked with Jack Carrington, the leading English Table Tennis Association coach of the day.

He became an ETTA staff coach in 1966 and went on to hold regional and national coaching posts for many years. As non-playing captain he led England's men at the 1979 World Championships, the European Championships of 1977-78 and 1981-82 and the 1983 Commonwealth Championships.

Away from the bench he sat on the association's Coaching and Schools Committee from 1966 to 1978, its Selection Committee from 1968 to 1984 and its Coaching Committee from 1984 to 1987. He wrote three books on the game, Play Better Table Tennis (1973), Successful Table Tennis (1980) and How to Play Table Tennis (1981), and contributed to the magazine Table Tennis News.

As a player Simpson represented Leeds in Yorkshire county competitions. He won the Leeds closed men's singles in 1968-69 and the men's doubles three times, in 1957-58 and 1960-61 with John Spencer and again in 1968-69.

He was made a vice-president of Table Tennis England and of the Yorkshire County TTA in 2024, the national honour recognising his service as northern staff coach and national team coach. He was a member of the Swaythling Club International and attended the national championships in 2025.
